evidence.title: Choe Deok-sin

evidence.title: Choe Deok-sin
evidence.text: After the military coup, from 1961 to 1963, Choe served as a Foreign Minister and Ambassador to West Germany.

evidence.title: Peder Hansen (politician)
evidence.text: Peder Hansen( 28 December 1859 – ??) was a Norwegian politician for the Moderate Liberal Party.

evidence.title: Peder Hansen (politician)
evidence.text: He was born at Hage in Fuse as a son of farmers Hans Johannesen Hage and Gurine Nilsdatter.

evidence.title: Peder Hansen (politician)
evidence.text: He started his professional career as a smith at the shipyard Laksevaag maskin- og jernskibsbyggeri in 1877.

evidence.title: Peder Hansen (politician)
evidence.text: In 1894 he advanced to foreman.

evidence.title: Peder Hansen (politician)
evidence.text: From 1904 to 1911 he lived as a merchant in Kristiania, but in 1911 he settled as a farmer.

evidence.title: Peder Hansen (politician)
evidence.text: He was a member of Askøen municipal council, and also served as an elector while Norway had such a political system.

evidence.title: Peder Hansen (politician)
evidence.text: He was elected to the Parliament of Norway in 1900.

evidence.title: Peder Hansen (politician)
evidence.text: He served one term for the constituency of Søndre Bergenhus Amt before being a deputy representative during the term 1904 – 1906.

evidence.title: Peder Hansen (politician)
evidence.text: Together with Hedvig Johannesen he had the daughter Ella Hage Hanssen( 1900 – 1991), a painter who married zoologist and oceanographer Albert Eide Parr, a son of scholar Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr.

evidence.title: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr
evidence.text: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr (13 May 1862 – 12 August 1935) was a Norwegian educator and psychologist.

evidence.title: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr
evidence.text: He was born in Drøbak as a son of ship-owner Hans Henry Parr and Laura Jørgensen.

evidence.title: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr
evidence.text: In March 1897 in Bergen he married Helga Johanne Eide, a daughter of consul Ludolf Eide and sister of Egil Eide.

evidence.title: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr
evidence.text: The couple had the son Albert Eide Parr, a noted zoologist and oceanographer who married a daughter of Peder Hansen.

evidence.title: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr
evidence.text: Parr finished Kristiania Commerce School in 1877, worked in an office for four years and from 1882 to 1883 he studied for, and took, the examen artium.

evidence.title: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr
evidence.text: He enrolled at the Royal Frederick University, and after one year of studying theology he switched to philology and graduated with the cand.philol. degree in 1890.

evidence.title: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr
evidence.text: He was hired as a teacher at Tanks Upper Secondary School in 1892 and Bergen Cathedral School in 1900.

evidence.title: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr
evidence.text: He retired for health reasons in 1929.

evidence.title: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr
evidence.text: He was a modern pedagogical thinker for his time, and wrote prolifically in "SamtidenVor Ungdom" and "Skolebladet" as well as the newspaper "Bergens Tidende".

evidence.title: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr
evidence.text: He also became known a pamphlet in 1918, in which he tried to counter the ideas of the comprehensive school whose inception was prepared by a special committee at that time.

evidence.title: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr
evidence.text: He was also interested in moral and psychology, and publicly debated these subjects from the 1890s.

evidence.title: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr
evidence.text: From 1899 to 1900 he conducted a study travel to Germany.

evidence.title: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr
evidence.text: In 1912 he issued the book "Følelsesbetoningens intellektuelle egenverdi".

evidence.title: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr
evidence.text: It was later expanded into a German-language thesis, "Der intellektuelle Eigenwert der Gefühlsbetonung" in 1922, but already in 1913 he successfully submitted the dissertation for the dr.philos. degree.

evidence.title: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr
evidence.text: He also published academically in French and English.

evidence.title: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr
evidence.text: He was hired as a part-time lecturer at Bergen Museum, and from 1917 he was a fellow of the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters.

evidence.title: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr
evidence.text: He was described as a "noble character" who dedicated himself to counter all forms of cheating and promote academic honesty.

evidence.title: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr
evidence.text: At the same time he was derided for his "exaggerated, nervously determined diligence" and "pathological self-criticism".

evidence.title: Thomas Johannes Lauritz Parr
evidence.text: He died in August 1935 in Bergen.
